title: Stord acquires AMS Fulfillment
sum: Stord has acquired AMS Fulfillment, a third-party logistics provider, in its largest acquisition to date. The sources do not state a price.
who: Fulfillment network and commerce technology provider founded in 2015 that serves independent commerce brands.
Third-party logistics provider for premium beauty, wellness and high-velocity direct-to-consumer brands, with more than 20 years of experience.
why: The deal adds more than 10 million annual orders and facilities in the Los Angeles, Salt Lake City and Philadelphia areas, and takes Stord's network to more than 100 locations. It is Stord's twelfth acquisition, following Shipwire from CMA CGM, Ware2Go from UPS and Pitney Bowes' e-commerce fulfillment business. Stord said some AMS facilities already use automated put walls and sortation systems.

parties.name: Stord
parties.size: More than 100 network locations; more than 1,000 brands

history.t: Raised $250 million Series F in May at a $3 billion valuation and launched Stord Labs
Secured a $400 million credit facility led by Citi in October
Acquired AMS Fulfillment, its twelfth acquisition

note: Price and closing date not stated in the sources.

title: MAK Acquisition terminates UniUni deal
sum: MAK Acquisition Corp. terminated its May 15, 2026 purchase agreement with Uni Express Inc. (UniUni) and Jun Wei (Peter) Lu. MAK said UniUni breached an interim covenant that set a maximum cumulative pre-tax loss.
who: A Cayman Islands special purpose acquisition corporation listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange that completed its IPO in October 2025.
The company that was to be taken public through a reverse take-over with MAK.
why: MAK said it sent a notice of breach on September 24, 2026 and that the 15-business-day cure period expired on October 19, 2026 without the breach being cured. MAK said it reserves all of its rights and will keep searching for a qualifying acquisition. MAK also said it is withdrawing its preliminary long form non-offering prospectus and will not file a final prospectus.

history.t: Completed its initial public offering in October 2025 and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Signed a purchase agreement with MAK on May 15, 2026; MAK terminated it on October 20, 2026.

title: WWEX Group and Auctane merge as ShipStation Global
sum: WWEX Group and Auctane completed a merger to create ShipStation Global, combining a freight brokerage and carrier network with parcel software. Terms were not disclosed.
who: Parcel software company behind the ShipStation brand.
why: The deal joins a freight brokerage with parcel software under the ShipStation brand. Dealroom said the combined company describes itself as the first multi-modal shipping platform for small and mid-size shippers and scaling enterprises. The network moves more than 3 billion shipments a year, according to Dealroom. In October 2026 ShipStation Global was named to FreightWaves' 2027 FreightTech 100 list.
note: Merger completion date and terms not stated in the source.

title: DHL eCommerce buys Venipak Baltic companies
target: Venipak Lietuva, Venipak Latvija and Venipak Eesti
sum: DHL eCommerce International Holdings is acquiring Venipak's Lithuanian, Latvian and Estonian companies. Lithuania's competition authority approved the deal on Wednesday, according to MLex.
who: Acquiring entity in the deal, part of the DHL eCommerce business.
Parcel delivery and freight transport company in Lithuania.
Parcel delivery and freight transport company in Latvia.
Parcel delivery and freight transport company in Estonia.
why: The deal covers parcel delivery and freight transport companies in all three Baltic states. Lithuania's competition authority has approved it. The source summary does not give a price, a closing date or the status of other regulatory approvals.
note: Based on a brief MLex summary; the full article was behind a paywall.

title: Duncan Solutions sells Pioneer Credit Recovery
sum: Duncan Solutions completed the sale of Pioneer Credit Recovery, Inc. after earlier 2026 sales of Pioneer Customer Experience and Gila. The buyer was not named and financial terms were not disclosed.
who: Provider of technology and services for government parking, tolling and camera-enforcement programs, founded in 1936.
Former affiliated business of Duncan that operated under Business Processing Solutions, LLC.
Los Angeles-based private equity firm founded in 2018 that invests in technology, business services and industrial companies.
why: The sale is the final divestiture in a restructuring that separates Duncan's transportation technology operations from its former affiliated businesses. Duncan, Pioneer, PCX and Gila were acquired by affiliates of Gallant Capital Partners in February 2025 through a carve-out of Navient's Government Services business, and the four previously operated under Business Processing Solutions, LLC. Truist Securities served as exclusive financial advisor to BPS on the three divestitures, according to the announcement.

title: Evri Group acquires Cross Border Connect
sum: Evri Group has agreed to acquire Cross Border Connect, a US-based logistics enablement provider specializing in delivery and returns. Financial terms were not disclosed.
who: Parcel delivery group that said it serves customers moving parcels between the UK, Europe and the US.
Boca Raton, Florida-based platform for international merchants entering the US market, with six US ports of entry and end-to-end customs clearance.
why: Evri said the acquisition supports its ability to serve customers on the UK-US trade lane and expands solutions for retailers, marketplaces and logistics partners trading across borders. It follows Evri's 2025 acquisition of Coll-8. Evri said Coll-8's customs clearance expertise and CBC's US logistics and technology capabilities create a more comprehensive cross-border offering.
note: Chris Lentjes, CBC co-founder and CEO, will continue to lead the business.

title: C.H. Robinson buys RXO for $5.8B
sum: C.H. Robinson Worldwide plans to acquire RXO in a stock-and-cash transaction valued at $5.8 billion. The companies announced the deal in a news release on Monday.
who: Third-party logistics company offering global, multimodal services; Dave Bozeman is president and CEO.
Provider of brokerage and transportation services, including expedited and last-mile services in North America; Drew Wilkerson is chairman and CEO.
why: According to the companies, the combination would create a third-party logistics company with over $25 billion in size, serving approximately 93,000 shippers and 600,000 carriers. C.H. Robinson said it would deploy its "Lean AI" operating model across RXO's workflows, targeting $300 million of net run-rate savings within two years of closing. According to an investor presentation, RXO has limited shipper overlap with C.H. Robinson. C.H. Robinson CFO Damon Lee said Navisphere would become the core system of record for RXO's overlapping truckload and less-than-truckload services.
note: Expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and RXO shareholder approval.
